about: Christina M. Coleman is the founder of the Law Offices of Christina M. Coleman, APC and represents employees, consumers, and businesses in California in matters of wrongful termination, discrimination, harassment, retaliation, wage and hour violations, civil rights violations, wrongful death, business disputes, and personal injury, and whistleblower cases. With more than two decades of experience, she has handled many high-profile cases, including employment discrimination and wrongful termination, sexual assault, civil rights disputes, real estate disputes, high-end weddings gone bad, breach of contract and fraud.

As an extremely skilled negotiator and litigator, Ms. Coleman is a member of the California Employment Lawyers Association (CELA), the Los Angeles Trial Lawyers’ Charities (LATLC), the Consumer Attorneys of California (CAOC), and has served on the Board of Governors for the Consumer Attorneys Association of Los Angeles (CAALA) since January 2018. In 2010, she was a finalist for the Streetfighter of the Year award from the Consumer Attorneys of California and was a finalist in 2008 for the Consumer Attorney of the Year from the same organization. A frequent writer and lecturer, Ms. Coleman shares her law experience in places such as Pepperdine University School of Law, The Advocate, The Forum, and conferences for CAALA, CELA and other organizations.

Admitted to practice in all of California’s state courts, the California Supreme Court, the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, and the U.S. District Courts for the Central and Southern Districts of California, Ms. Coleman’s career started with a Bachelor of Arts in linguistics from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1993. She then earned a Juris Doctor from the University of San Diego School of Law in 1997.

In the past, Ms. Coleman has proven her knowledge and experience with several cases that ended in upwards of a million dollars in settlements and verdicts, including an 8-million-dollar legal malpractice case.
